messages:
FinServe SRE: Hey team — in prod our websocket streams to Redwood keep getting silent after ~90-120s, client still connected but no chunks arrive. Happens across multiple customers behind the same corporate gateway.
Priya Patel: Thanks, sorry you're hitting this. Can you confirm if the stream socket stays ESTABLISHED on your side when it goes silent?
FinServe SRE: Yes TCP stays ESTABLISHED. App side sees no data for ~2m then eventually a subtle reconnect. No TLS errors.
Carlos Mendez: Sounds like a middlebox idle-buffering or NAT session refresh. Is your egress via a proxy/NAT appliance?
FinServe SRE: Yes, corporate firewall + outbound NAT SNAT pool and an inline security device (vendor: DeepGate). They have a 120s idle TCP session policy.
Elliot Zhang: Okay that aligns. Two common triggers: (1) middlebox buffers small chunks and doesn't forward until buffer full or idle close, (2) device sends a TCP RST after idle. Do you see RST?
FinServe SRE: We don't see RST client-side. We captured a short packet trace — looks like keepalives not traversing. Will paste tcpdump.
FinServe SRE: ```
15:12:01.123456 IP client->redwood  TCP 1000 flags [P.] seq 123 ack 456 win 29200
15:13:41.654321 IP client->redwood  TCP 40 flags [. ] ack 789 win 29184  # no payload, maybe keepalive
15:13:41.654333 IP ??? -> client  TCP 0 flags []  # no obvious RST
```
Carlos Mendez: Interesting — if device drops or holds on small frames (tiny websocket frames / TLS records) it can seem like silence. Two quick mitigations: (A) enable app-level websocket pings at <60s interval, (B) use TCP keepalive with interval < idle timeout.
Priya Patel: Also check if TLS record size is tiny. Some middleboxes aggregate TLS records before forwarding. Does your client send single-byte application messages?
FinServe SRE: Our client sends incremental tokens (small bytes) during streaming. We can batch but would prefer server-side solution.
Elliot Zhang: On Redwood side we can send periodic 15s padding frames for streaming sessions—small harmless bytes to keep middleboxes from buffering. Before we change anything, can you confirm your egress allowlist includes our streaming endpoint IPs and that SNI is preserved (no TLS interception)?
FinServe SRE: Egress allowlist includes *.redwood-inference.com and IP ranges listed in our onboarding doc. The inline device is not doing TLS MITM (no cert reissue), but it does inspect packet sizes.
Priya Patel: Two repro asks: (1) a short tcpdump pcap covering the silent window, (2) sample client log showing websocket frames/events, (3) confirm NAT session timeout setting on appliance. Can you share those?
FinServe SRE: Uploading pcap to secure share now. NAT timeout is 120s per vendor doc.
SupportBot: Incident created - #INC-2026-984, priority P2, assigned to eng-sre.
Carlos Mendez: Thanks. Quick triage plan: (1) ask runtime to try short padding/ping change as a canary, (2) ask customer to enable client websocket ping or TCP keepalive, (3) recommend vendor change to NAT timeout or allow small TLS records immediate forwarding.
Elliot Zhang: I can push a safe canary that adds 1 byte of padding every 30s for streaming sessions from our edge in the affected region. It's opt-in per customer. Would you like us to enable for your workspace?
FinServe SRE: Please enable for our workspace, that'd be ideal for now. We'll work with security vendor to update NAT behavior.
Priya Patel: Enabling canary now. ETA ~20m. I'll follow up with test steps: after enable, open a stream that emits small chunks every 10s and confirm no silent window.
FinServe SRE: Copy that. Appreciate fast response.
Carlos Mendez: Post-canary, if you still see silence, we'll ask for full pcap and may run a proxy in between to reproduce. Also consider raising kernel TCP keepalive lower than 60s on clients.
Elliot Zhang: Note for internal: add doc snippet to support KB about middlebox buffering vs NAT idle: include websocket ping, TCP keepalive, TLS record padding.
Priya Patel: Closing loop once canary verification done. :handshake:
